checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-EXT-TRACE-REQUEST: Trace Request Input Validation and DoS Prevention
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Identify the trace API endpoint handler that receives external trace requests. 2. Verify that the transaction hash parameter is validated against a canonical format (32-byte hex) before any DB lookup. 3. Confirm that non-existent transaction hashes return an error without triggering expensive EVM re-execution. 4. Check for resource bounding: confirm there is a timeout or gas/step limit on traced execution to prevent an attacker from requesting traces of extremely gas-intensive transactions. 5. Verify rate limiting or authentication exists on the trace endpoint. 6. Attempt to submit a trace request with an invalid hash, an extremely long hash, and a hash referencing a maximally complex transaction to observe resource consumption.
executable_checks: Send trace request with invalid transaction hash format; verify rejection before DB lookup
Send trace request for non-existent transaction; verify no EVM execution is triggered
Send trace request for gas-intensive transaction; verify timeout or resource cap is enforced
Measure memory/CPU usage during trace of complex transaction; confirm bounded growth
checklist.notes: Boundary property. Source: PROP-W1-EIP3155-PRECOND-002. Primary element: EDGE-EXT-TRACE-REQUEST. Trust model data not found for this edge — no trust model partial defines EDGE-EXT-TRACE-REQUEST, so boundary validation focuses on generic input validation and DoS prevention. Related assumption: ASSUM-EIP3155-01.

checklist.title: Verify Resource Exhaustion Mitigation After Trace Request Crosses Boundary
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Examine the code path from trace request reception to EVM execution. 2. Verify that STATE-RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION-RISK is explicitly handled: check for gas limits, step counters, memory caps, or execution timeouts applied during traced execution. 3. Confirm that exceeding any resource bound aborts the trace cleanly without crashing the node. 4. Test by requesting a trace for a transaction that performs maximum memory expansion or deep call stacks.
executable_checks: Request trace of transaction with maximum memory expansion; verify node stability
Request trace of transaction with deep call stack; verify bounded execution
Verify trace abortion on resource limit produces clean error response
checklist.notes: Supporting node check for boundary property PROP-W1-EIP3155-PRECOND-002. Validates internal handling of resource risks after data crosses the trust boundary.

checklist.title: Falsify STOP Opcode Error Trace Suppression Rule
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Locate the trace output generation logic, specifically the handler for ACTION-CHECK-STOP-ERROR. 2. Create a test transaction where STOP opcode encounters an error condition (e.g., out-of-gas exactly at STOP). 3. Execute trace and verify NO trace line is emitted for the STOP opcode. 4. Create a test transaction where a non-STOP opcode (e.g., ADD, CALL) encounters an error. 5. Verify the trace line IS emitted and contains the 'error' field. 6. Attempt edge case: trigger error on the opcode immediately preceding STOP to verify STOP itself is still suppressed.
executable_checks: Trace transaction with error on STOP; verify no trace line for STOP
Trace transaction with error on non-STOP opcode; verify trace line with error field exists
Verify edge case: error before STOP does not leak STOP trace line
checklist.notes: Internal post-condition. Source: PROP-W1-EIP3155-POSTCOND-001. Falsification target: ACTION-CHECK-STOP-ERROR. Mindset: Formal Verification Engineer.

checklist.title: Falsify gasCost Field Computation as gas_before - gas_after
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Locate ACTION-COMPUTE-GAS-COST in the tracer implementation. 2. Identify how gas_before and gas_after are captured relative to opcode execution. 3. Design test transactions with opcodes of known gas costs (e.g., ADD=3, SLOAD=2100 cold). 4. Execute trace and compare each trace line's gasCost against (gas_before - gas_after). 5. Test with opcodes that have variable gas costs (CALL with value transfer, SSTORE with different storage states). 6. Attempt to falsify: find an opcode where refunds or stipends might cause gasCost != gas_before - gas_after.
executable_checks: Trace transaction with ADD opcode; verify gasCost == 3
Trace transaction with cold SLOAD; verify gasCost == 2100
Trace CALL with value transfer; verify gasCost accounts for stipend correctly
Trace SSTORE with refund scenario; verify gasCost reflects actual consumption, not net
checklist.notes: Internal post-condition. Source: PROP-W1-EIP3155-POSTCOND-003. Falsification target: ACTION-COMPUTE-GAS-COST.

checklist.title: Falsify Re-Approval Requires Full Re-Evaluation After Origin Removal
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Locate the origin approval and removal logic. 2. Identify the ACTION-REAPPLY code path. 3. Remove an origin from the approved list due to a requirement violation. 4. Attempt to re-approve the origin: verify it goes through the FULL evaluation process (same as initial approval). 5. Check for cached approval states, fast-path re-approvals, or any mechanism that bypasses full re-evaluation. 6. Test: modify the origin to still violate requirements and attempt re-approval; confirm rejection.

Check for cached approval state after removal; confirm cache is cleared
Re-apply origin still violating requirements; verify rejection
checklist.notes: Internal post-condition. Source: PROP-W1-EIP5757-POSTCOND-001. Falsification target: ACTION-REAPPLY.

checklist.title: Falsify Difficulty Bomb Fake Block Number Computation (offset 10,700,000)
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Locate ACTION-COMPUTE-FAKE-BLOCK-NUMBER in the difficulty calculation code. 2. Verify the offset subtracted is exactly 10,700,000. 3. Test with block numbers: 10,699,999 (fake < 0, should be 0), 10,700,000 (fake = 0), 10,700,001 (fake = 1), and a large number like 11,000,000. 4. For each, verify bomb component = 2^((fake_block_number // 100000) - 2). 5. Specifically test negative fake_block_number handling: confirm it is clamped to 0, not wrapped as unsigned. 6. Test integer overflow: use maximum possible block number and verify no overflow in the exponent calculation.

Compute at block 10,700,000; verify fake_block_number = 0, bomb = 2^(-2) = 0
Compute at block 11,000,000; verify fake = 300,000, bomb = 2^(3-2) = 2
Verify no integer overflow at maximum block number
checklist.notes: Internal post-condition. Source: PROP-W1-ARROW-GLACIER-POSTCOND-001. Related ambiguity: AMB-ARROW-GLACIER-01.

checklist.title: Falsify Account Emptiness Definition Excludes Storage State

Attempt to falsify: create an account with nonce=0, balance=0, empty code, but non-empty storage. Verify it IS classified as empty. 4. Test: account with nonce=1, balance=0, empty code — must NOT be empty. 5. Test: account with nonce=0, balance=1 wei, empty code — must NOT be empty. 6. Test: account with nonce=0, balance=0, non-empty code — must NOT be empty. 7. Confirm storage is never consulted in the emptiness check.
executable_checks: Account with zero nonce/balance/code but non-empty storage; verify classified as empty
Account with nonce=1; verify NOT empty
Account with balance=1; verify NOT empty
Account with non-empty code; verify NOT empty

Test edge values: condition = 1, condition = -1 (max uint256), condition = 2^256-1.

Test with consecutive PUSH instructions where data bytes could be misinterpreted as opcodes. 6. Attempt to JUMP to a 0x5b within PUSH data; verify execution reverts with invalid jump destination.

Test duplicate address entries: verify FULL cost is charged for duplicates (no deduplication discount). 7. Test duplicate storage keys: verify full cost charged.

1 address, 0 keys; verify += 2400

checklist.title: Falsify Block Propagation Delay Within Sompolinsky-Zohar Security Bounds
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Locate ACTION-MEASURE-PROPAGATION-DELAY or equivalent network monitoring. 2. Understand the security bound: beta/lambda >= 1/(1 + D*lambda). 3. Create blocks with increasing calldata sizes (up to block gas limit). 4. Measure propagation delay D for each size. 5. Verify D remains within bounds such that the security inequality holds. 6. Attempt to falsify: craft a maximally-sized calldata block and measure if propagation delay exceeds the security threshold.

Measure propagation delay for maximum calldata block
Verify security inequality holds for max-calldata scenario
